sprint: Magic Publish — Sprint M4 (Magic Animation). Per docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ROADMAP.md: "Bring pages to life. This sprint is entirely about delight. Extend ReelComposer to support crossfade, fade, gentle scale, and soft movement. Avoid flashy effects. Everything should feel storybook-like." Animation language: Background -> wash in / Objects -> fade + rise / Text -> draw word-by-word / Final page -> pause. Deliverables: New transition mode / Animation timing / Animation configuration. Success criteria: a single page feels magical without showing editor UI.
task: The central insight, and the reason this ship is small: consecutive reveal frames are pixel-identical EXCEPT for what just arrived, so a plain crossfade already reads as "only the new thing appeared" — every unchanged pixel blends to itself and does not move. The obvious alternative (render each arrival onto its own layer and animate that) was considered and rejected: it would allocate another ~8 MB canvas per stage boundary, directly undoing M3's memory-cleanup deliverable. js/reelComposer.js gains two painters beside the existing paintPageTurn — paintWash (a pure crossfade over black, eased with easeInOutSine) and paintRise (a crossfade plus a small lift, easeOutCubic) — plus a TRANSITIONS dispatch table and a per-page resolver so a page's own transition/transitionMs wins over the reel-wide default, which is what lets ONE reel turn between pages and wash, rise or draw within them; Story Reel's existing transition:'page-turn' is untouched and keeps working. Rise ghosting (drawing the incoming frame at an offset briefly doubles unchanged content against itself) is mitigated by RISE_SETTLE=0.45, which spends the lift entirely while the incoming frame is still faint: easeOutCubic(t)=0.45 at t~0.181, where incoming alpha is 0.45, so the lift is over while the frame is under half-visible. MIN_PAGE_HOLD_MS 300 becomes MIN_FRAME_MS 60, inert for existing callers (Story Reel's own floor is 1500) and necessary because a word frame is ~140ms. Word-by-word could NOT live in the composer — a crossfade between "no text" and "all the text" has no way to produce the words in between, and a clip-rect cannot follow words across a line wrap without clipping everything else on the page — so the intermediate frames have to exist as rendered slides, which is js/magicReveal.js's job: the Words beat expands into up to MAX_WORD_STEPS=8 steps at WORD_HOLD_MS=140 each, the cap being a real memory budget rather than a rate (every step is a genuine full-size canvas). Text sources fill in PARALLEL (every source to the same word fraction) rather than sequentially — identical on the common single-block page, and "the words are appearing" reads better than one block completing before the next starts. Scene blueprint text-holders (Cover/Hook/End) are deliberately NOT truncated: their content resolves through SceneEngine's own text sources rather than sitting on the element, so they arrive whole with the first word step — a disclosed limitation, since those pages carry a title, not prose. Every stage now also carries `kind` ('blank'|'world'|'artwork'|'decorations'|'text'), which is the only thing M4 needed from that module beyond the stages themselves; the Finished stage carries the LAST group's id rather than 'finished', because the finished frame IS that beat arriving. js/storyDestinations.js tags each frame via _magicTransition(stage, frameIndex, pageIndex): the very first frame of the story washes up out of black (there is no page behind it to turn away), a later page is turned to, and within a page nothing turns — the page is assembling in front of you, so arrivals rise and words draw. The format's reel-wide default moves from the M3 placeholder 'none' to 'page-turn' as the safe reading for any frame that somehow arrives untagged. A stage-index vs frame-index drift was caught before running anything: encodePage `continue`s past a stage without a slide, so the tagger takes frames.length rather than the loop index. js/publishStudio.js needed no changes at all (a frame simply carries a transition alongside its bitmap and hold) and renderer/slideRenderer.js was not touched, so Museum Gallery's canonical hashes are not the gate for this ship. Verified 41/41 via magic_m4_verify: the composer vocabulary and its timings; wash is a real crossfade AND — decisively — UNCHANGED content does not move or double (a shared black square stays black and shared white background stays white at every t, which is the whole reason a plain crossfade reads as an arrival); rise puts the incoming frame below its place early, lands it by mid-transition, and spends the lift while the frame is still under 0.6 alpha (the anti-ghosting design, measured rather than asserted); a mixed reel composes and unknown/zero-length transitions degrade to a hard cut rather than throwing; every stage is tagged in beat order with the finished frame tagged as the last beat; the Words beat accumulates ('Once' / 'Once upon' / 'Once upon a'), the last step IS the caller's own slide, a 12-word page caps at 8 steps starting at 'one two', a 2-word page takes 2, and revealStages still never mutates the caller's slide; frame 0 of page 0 washes while page 1 turns and no other frame turns; and a real publish through the actual UI reaches Celebration with a blob checked at the byte level (>20 KB, video/*, _magic.webm, EBML magic 1a45dfa3 read off the blob's own first four bytes). Four test-methodology bugs were found and fixed in the suite itself, none of them app bugs: the arriving block fades white->blue so BLUE is the wrong channel to watch (it is 255 at both ends) and RED is the one that travels; the fixture World places a full-bleed wash on EVERY page, so with it active no page is ever truly bare and the empty branch had to be exercised with the World silenced for one call; the wordy-page probe mapped ALL stages rather than the word steps, putting the blank and World frames ahead of them; and the end-to-end section used the wrong destination selectors and read _publishedBlob/_publishedFilename as properties when they are functions. Nine assertions across magic_m2_verify and magic_m3_verify were updated as the intended and disclosed consequence of word-by-word (a four-beat page yields eight stages, not five) rather than a regression — M2's B5 was rewritten to assert the real rule using the new `kind` (every beat gets at least one frame; only Words gets more than one), and M3's F1 now asserts the new reel-wide default. Regression: magic_m1 32/32, magic_m2 33/33, magic_m3 32/32, reel 15/15, reel_backdrop 10/10, reel_pageturn 12/12, voice 16/16, voice_note 22/22, both goldenBuilds PASS.
